            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>

                    <execution>

                        <phase>process-sources</phase>
                        <goals>

                        </configuration>

                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                    <args>
                        <arg>-Xjvm-default=all</arg>

             Kotlin declarations. Generate the javadoc jar with Dokka instead;
             the parent's maven-javadoc-plugin is skipped for this module only.

             profile and let the parent's maven-javadoc-plugin take over again. -->

            <id>release</id>
            <properties>
                <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
            </properties>
            <build>
                <plugins>
                    <plugin>
                        <groupId>org.jetbrains.dokka</groupId>
                        <artifactId>dokka-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                        <version>${dokka.version}</version>
                        <executions>
                            <execution>
                                <id>attach-javadocs</id>
                                <phase>package</phase>
                                <goals><goal>javadocJar</goal></goals>
                            </execution>
                        </executions>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirectories>
                                <dir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</dir>
                                <dir>${project.basedir}/src/main/java</dir>
                            </sourceDirectories>
                            <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                            <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                        </configuration>
                    </plugin>
                </plugins>
            </build>
        </profile>
    </profiles>
</project>

                <plugin>
                    <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                    <artifactId>quarkus-extension-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>${quarkus.version}</version>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.5.0</version>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
                    <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>${spring-boot.version}</version>
                </plugin>
            </plugins>
        </pluginManagement>
    </build>

    <!-- The JVM libraries are pure JVM: no Rust toolchain or cargo build is part of
         `mvn test`, `mvn package`, or the Maven Central release. Rust is only needed
         for the native desktop demos (scripts/lib.sh builds `libpathland_core` and the
         GTK/Qt renderer dylibs) and for regenerating shared artifacts (the protocol
         manifest, engine traces, HTML golden fixtures, and TS constants).

         Run BEFORE an IntelliJ IDE run: refreshes the generated layers the IDE cannot
         rebuild itself — the design CSS/tokens (npm build) and the DOM bundle
         (npm build:all) — plus the render-html module's embedded CSS resources (its
         Maven copy step does not run under IntelliJ's own build). IntelliJ then
         compiles the Java modules from its module outputs (the pathland modules are
         imported, so no ~/.m2 is used) and copies the refreshed bundle + its
         dom-renderer.current manifest into target/classes on Build Project. Invoke with
         `mvn -P refresh-ide validate`, then Reload All Maven Projects → Build → Run →
         reload. The bundle is content-hashed (dom-renderer-<sha256>.js) so a rebuilt
         bundle busts the immutable asset cache by URL — a normal reload after restart
         is enough, no hard refresh. -->
    <profiles>
    <!-- Default reactor: the libraries plus the demo applications. Maven deactivates
         an activeByDefault profile as soon as any other profile in this POM is
         activated, so `-P release`, `-P refresh-ide`, and `-P jvm-only` all leave a
         demo-free reactor. -->
    <profile>
        <id>demos</id>
        <activation>
            <activeByDefault>true</activeByDefault>
        </activation>
        <modules>
            <module>pathland-demo-views-kotlin</module>
            <module>pathland-desktop-demo</module>
            <module>pathland-quarkus-demo</module>
            <module>pathland-spring-boot-demo</module>
        </modules>
    </profile>
    <!-- `mvn -Pjvm-only test`: the JVM libraries and server starters only. Activating
         this profile deactivates the default-active `demos` profile, so no demo
         modules are in the reactor. The JVM libraries never required Rust. -->
    <profile>
        <id>jvm-only</id>
        <properties>
            <pathland.jvm-only>true</pathland.jvm-only>
        </properties>
    </profile>
    <!-- Maven Central publishing (`mvn -P release deploy`). Normal builds/tests are
         unaffected: this profile only activates on demand. Because it is active, the
         default `demos` profile is off and the reactor contains only publishable
         modules. -->
    <profile>
        <id>release</id>
        <build>
            <plugins>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.3.1</version>
                    <executions>
                        <execution>
                            <id>attach-sources</id>
                            <goals><goal>jar-no-fork</goal></goals>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.6.3</version>
                    <configuration>
                        <!-- Central requires a -javadoc jar; disable strict doclint so
                             existing doc comments don't fail the release build.
                             Don't link to reactor siblings' apidocs: pathland-view-core
                             builds its javadoc with Dokka, so target/apidocs does not
                             exist and javadoc logs "Error fetching link" noise. -->
                        <doclint>none</doclint>
                        <detectOfflineLinks>false</detectOfflineLinks>
                    </configuration>
                    <executions>
                        <execution>
                            <id>attach-javadocs</id>
                            <goals><goal>jar</goal></goals>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-gpg-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.2.4</version>
                    <executions>
                        <execution>
                            <id>sign-artifacts</id>
                            <phase>verify</phase>
                            <goals><goal>sign</goal></goals>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>
                <!-- Uploads the whole reactor to the Sonatype Central Portal as one
                     deployment (auto-published after validation). Credentials come
                     from the `central` server in ~/.m2/settings.xml. -->
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.sonatype.central</groupId>
                    <artifactId>central-publishing-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>0.6.0</version>
                    <extensions>true</extensions>
                    <configuration>
                        <publishingServerId>central</publishingServerId>
                        <autoPublish>true</autoPublish>
                    </configuration>
                </plugin>
            </plugins>
        </build>
    </profile>
    <profile>
        <id>refresh-ide</id>
        <build>
            <plugins>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId>
                    <artifactId>exec-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.1.0</version>
                    <!-- Runs ONLY at the aggregator (parent); the refresh steps must
                         not repeat once per child module. -->
                    <inherited>false</inherited>
                    <executions>
                        <execution>
                            <id>refresh-design</id>
                            <phase>validate</phase>
                            <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                            <configuration>
                                <workingDirectory>${session.executionRootDirectory}/../../design</workingDirectory>
                                <executable>npm</executable>
                                <arguments>
                                    <argument>run</argument>
                                    <argument>build</argument>
                                </arguments>
                            </configuration>
                        </execution>
                        <execution>
                            <id>refresh-design-sync</id>
                            <phase>validate</phase>
                            <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                            <configuration>
                                <workingDirectory>${session.executionRootDirectory}/../..</workingDirectory>
                                <executable>${session.executionRootDirectory}/../../scripts/sync-design-css.sh</executable>
                            </configuration>
                        </execution>
                        <execution>
                            <id>refresh-ts</id>
                            <phase>validate</phase>
                            <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                            <configuration>
                                <workingDirectory>${session.executionRootDirectory}/../typescript</workingDirectory>
                                <executable>npm</executable>
                                <arguments>
                                    <argument>run</argument>
                                    <argument>build:all</argument>
                                </arguments>
                            </configuration>
                        </execution>
                        <execution>
                            <id>refresh-render-html</id>
                            <phase>validate</phase>
                            <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                            <configuration>
                                <workingDirectory>${session.executionRootDirectory}</workingDirectory>
                                <executable>mvn</executable>
                                <arguments>
                                    <argument>-q</argument>
                                    <argument>-pl</argument>
                                    <argument>pathland-view-core,pathland-render-html</argument>
                                    <argument>process-resources</argument>
                                </arguments>
                            </configuration>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>
            </plugins>
        </build>
    </profile>
    </profiles>
</project>

# pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status **Last updated:** November 7, 2026 The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the Pathland protocol, written entirely in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter, signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, and the `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers. Server and renderer modules depend on this one module; Java hosts consume the Kotlin-authored views through JVM interop. JNA ring interop lives in the opt-in `pathland-native-core` module, so this module (and every server/native-image build) carries no JNA. ## Implemented - **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`, `Commands` (incl. `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`), `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`, `TokenPath`. - **Attributed text** (`dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString`): pure-Kotlin model + range-tracking builder (Kotlin char indices → UTF-8 byte offsets) and payload encode/decode; `Text(AttributedString)` / `Text(Signal)` emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` through the emitter and both sinks. - **Built-in inline Markdown**: `Text("...")` parses the v1 subset by default (`**bold**`/`__bold__`, `*italic*`/`_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `~~strikethrough~~`, `[label](url)`); `markdown = false` renders literal text. `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` is now a **pure-Java parser** (no native library, so it runs on every platform and under GraalVM native-image); it is a behavioural port of the Rust `pathland-markdown` crate (pre-scan + bounded cache). The Rust crate remains the parser for the Rust DSL and non-JVM hosts. Plain results use the compact `SET_TEXT` path; rich results emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`. Reactive `Text(Signal)` parses on change. - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/ `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState` during a component render. - **Topic subscriptions** (`dev.pathland.view.core.subscription`): a strongly typed `Topic` and the DSL `topic(key, subject, initial)` (also `Signals.topic`). Scoped topics name an entity subject; `Topic.global(name)` declares an unscoped `Topic` with the two-argument `topic(key, initial)` form. Both return a normal `Signal` backed by a session-local mirror; the server runtime registers it with the app's hub and applies published values on the session actor. `SessionContext` (thread-local, installed by `PathlandSession` around every actor task) also exposes `unsubscribe` and `submit`. Resolution is lazy when a root view's field initializer runs before the context is installed. - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and annotation processor are removed. - **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`, `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`. **Hardened (issue #63)**: `FrameCodec.parse` reads the attacker-controlled `opcodeCount`/`stringsLen` as unsigned `Long` values and validates them against the actual message length before allocating; string offsets are bounds-checked (`Parsed.stringAt`). parts.text:
I have enough context to form the plan, but there's significant ambiguity about scope. Let me ask clarifying questions.

Key decisions:
1. Does "core parts" mean packages `protocol`, `transport`, `signal`, `state`, `subscription` only? Or also `router`, `AttributedString`, action/event types? Or everything except `dev.pathland.view.dsl`?
2. Should the new `pathland-core` be pure Java (rewritten from Kotlin), while `pathland-view-core` retains Kotlin DSL + engine? Or should engine also move to pathland-core?
3. Should `dev.pathland.view.engine` (emitter) move? Note: "engine" in Rust is separate from core. The user says core classes vs UI dsl. Emitter is arguably core engine, not DSL.
4. Java package naming for new module: keep `dev.pathland.view.core` package names or rename to `dev.pathland.core`? Keeping package names avoids breaking imports downstream and makes split mechanical. But module artifact is pathland-core. If rewriting in Java, same packages are ideal.
5. Whether to preserve backward compatibility / keep pathland-view-core as a dependency aggregator (so downstream modules unchanged) or update all downstream poms.
6. Java version 17, no Kotlin in pathland-core.
7. Tests: move corresponding tests and port to Java.

Let me ask the user these questions with the question tool. Since multiple questions, I can ask up to... let's ask a few key ones.

But first let me understand more about what exactly is entangled. The core package `dev.pathland.view.core` contains both SPI/view vocabulary (View, Modified, Environment, MediaController, WindowMetadata, etc.) and "value types" like Color/Length/enums. Is that "core classes" or "UI DSL"? The user says "pathland-view-core has both core classes and UI dsl". Likely the whole `dev.pathland.view.core` (minus maybe DSL-internal views) + engine constitutes core, and `dev.pathland.view.dsl` is UI DSL. But the request "move core parts to java and separate module called pathland-core" suggests they want pathland-core to be Java core protocol/runtime, and pathland-view-core keeps DSL (Kotlin).

Potential target architecture:
- `pathland-core` (Java): protocol, transport, signal, state, subscription, router, attributed string? plus value types and SPI (View interface, Environment) - everything non-DSL.
- `pathland-view-core` (Kotlin): `dev.pathland.view.dsl` builders + `dev.pathland.view.engine` emitter (maybe). But engine depends heavily on core. Actually if engine is in view-core, it needs View SPI in core. That's fine: view-core depends on core.

But the engine is a core runtime, not UI DSL. Hmm. The Rust architecture has pathland-engine separate. In JVM, could keep engine in pathland-view-core or move to core. The user explicitly says "core parts to java and separate module called pathland-core" — engine is a core part. I think safest: ask.

Also, "move core parts to java" may mean literally converting Kotlin to Java. That's a lot: ~60 files. Need to confirm.

Let me ask 4-5 questions in one tool call.

Actually, the instructions say ask when weighing tradeoffs. Let me ask.

Let me also consider package/module naming conflict with Rust crates `pathland-core` (Rust) — but Java artifact `dev.pathland:pathland-core` is distinct. Fine.

Let me formulate questions:

Q1: Scope of "core": 
- Option A: Protocol/transport/signal/state/subscription only (minimal, keeps View SPI/engine/DSL in view-core)
- Option B: All non-DSL packages (protocol, transport, signal, state, subscription, router, core SPI/value types, AttributedString) — view-core keeps only `dev.pathland.view.dsl` + engine
- Option C: Everything except `dev.pathland.view.dsl`, including engine
Recommended B or C? I'd recommend B with engine kept in view-core? Hmm. Let me think about dependency direction. If core includes View SPI and Environment, then engine must depend on core (fine). If core does not include View SPI, engine stays with DSL. Actually the cleanest split: pathland-core = protocol + engine runtime + signals/state/router/SPI (everything needed to emit), pathland-view-core = DSL only. That matches Rust: pathland-core (protocol) + pathland-engine (emitter) + pathland-view (DSL). But request only mentions one new module pathland-core (Java). Maybe combine core+engine into pathland-core.

Wait "move core parts to java" could mean "move the core parts to [the] Java [language]" because currently all core is Kotlin. Then module pathland-core. In that case DSL remains Kotlin in pathland-view-core. The engine could be either.

Q2: Language: full Java rewrite of moved classes vs keep Kotlin? The phrase "to java" implies rewrite. Confirm.

Q3: Package naming: keep `dev.pathland.view.core.*` for moved classes (zero import churn downstream) vs rename to `dev.pathland.core.*`.

Q4: Downstream module artifact dependency: update all consumers to depend on pathland-core + pathland-view-core (view-core depends on core so consumers can keep view-core dependency), or add pathland-core as transitive. Recommended: view-core depends on core; other modules keep depending on view-core where they use DSL, but add explicit dependency where they only use core. Simpler: all existing poms keep pathland-view-core (which transitively exposes core). But for modules that only use core (state-redis? server-core uses both), could add core explicitly. We'll plan.

Q5: Engine location.

Let me ask a consolidated set. Use question tool with multiple questions. Options custom enabled. I can include recommended first.

Let me do 4 questions:
1. What belongs in pathland-core? (options)
2. Rewrite language? (Java rewrite vs keep Kotlin)
3. Package names? 
4. Engine placement? (maybe combined with #1)
5. Versioning/compat? Maybe not.

Let me combine engine into scope question. Options:
A. Protocol/transport/signal/state/subscription/router/AttributedString/SPI + engine = all non-DSL (Recommended)
B. Only protocol/transport/signal/state/subscription
C. All non-DSL except engine (engine stays view-core)
D. Everything including DSL? no.

Actually "core classes" vs "UI dsl" — engine is not DSL. I'd recommend A. But the engine is named `dev.pathland.view.engine` and depends on View, Environment (SPI). If we put engine in pathland-core, then core contains UI-ish view vocabulary. That's okay — like a view engine.

Hmm, but the user might intend `pathland-view-core` to become the UI DSL module including engine. Let's ask.

Let me also check whether there's a build/test script or CI referencing pathland-view-core. The plan will mention updating all poms and AGENTS etc.

Also important for GraalVM: the current Java stack uses JNA to load dylibs embedded in jars. Under GraalVM native-image, that dylib still needs to be present at runtime (native-image doesn't embed/extract the jar resource unless configured via `-H:IncludeResources`; JNA's `Native.load` with an absolute path works, but the `extractEmbedded` mechanism relies on classpath resources and `getResourceAsStream`; in native-image resources must be registered). Also important for GraalVM: the current Java stack uses JNA to load dylibs embedded in jars. Under GraalVM native-image, that dylib still needs to be present at runtime (native-image doesn't embed/extract the jar resource unless configured via `-H:IncludeResources`; JNA's `Native.load` with an absolute path works, but the `extractEmbedded` mechanism relies on classpath resources and `getResourceAsStream`; in native-image resources must be registered). If protocol + HTML renderer were pure Kotlin/Java, then GraalVM native-image could compile everything ahead-of-time into a single static-ish executable: no JNA, no dylib extraction, no JNI. That's a real benefit. Downside: duplicate implementation, divergence risk, maintenance, and the Rust renderer is 4.7k lines with golden tests; Kotlin implementation would need to be rebuilt and kept byte-identical? 7: internal abstract class ReactiveNode(
8:     @JvmField val name: String?,
9: ) {
10:     /** A producer edge: the producer node plus its version when this node last read it. */
11:     internal class ProducerEdge(@JvmField val node: ReactiveNode) {
12:         @JvmField var lastSeenVersion: Long = node.version
13:     }
14: 
15:     @JvmField val producers: MutableList<ProducerEdge> = ArrayList()
16:     @JvmField val consumers: MutableList<ReactiveNode> = ArrayList()
17: 
18:     /** Bumped when this node's own value changes. */
19:     @JvmField var version: Long = 0
20: 
21:     /** Whether this node must (re)evaluate. */
22:     @JvmField var dirty: Boolean = true
23: 
24:     /** Whether the evaluation function has run at least once. */
25:     @JvmField var firstRun: Boolean = true
26: 
27:     /** Whether this node may write signals during its evaluation. */
28:     @JvmField var allowSignalWrites: Boolean = false
29: 
30:     /** Cached evaluation error (computed) / last run error (effect). */
31:     @JvmField var error: Throwable? = null
32: 
33:     fun describe(): String = name ?: javaClass.simpleName
34: 
35:     /** Register a dependency from the current reactive context to `this`. */
36:     fun recordDependency() {
37:         val consumer = ReactiveContext.current() ?: return
38:         val idx = consumer.indexOfProducer(this)
39:         if (idx < 0) {
40:             consumer.producers.add(ProducerEdge(this))
41:             consumers.add(consumer)
42:         } else {
43:             consumer.producers[idx].lastSeenVersion = version
44:         }
45:     }
46: 
47:     private fun indexOfProducer(producer: ReactiveNode): Int =
48:         producers.indexOfFirst { it.node === producer }
49: 
50:     /** True when at least one producer's version differs from what this node observed. */
51:     fun depsChanged(): Boolean = producers.any { it.node.version != it.lastSeenVersion }
52: 
53:     /** Drop all producer edges. */
54:     fun resetProducers() {
55:         for (edge in producers) {
56:             edge.node.consumers.remove(this)
57:         }
58:         producers.clear()
59:     }

62:     fun refreshProducers() {
63:         for (edge in producers) {

package dev.pathland.view.core.subscription

/**
 * A strongly typed, always-scoped subscription key.
 *
 * [T] is the published payload type and [S] is the subject (the thing the
 * subscription is about — a customer id, order id, tenant, conversation, …).
 * Both are checked at compile time by [subscribe] and
 * `PathlandSignalHub.publish`.
 *
 * Identity is by [name] (not by instance), so a topic declared once and shared
 * across modules — or across a process boundary — resolves to the same
 * subscription stream. Two topics with the same name must therefore carry the
 * same payload and subject types; declare each topic once in a shared constant
 * object.
 */
class Topic<T, S>(@JvmField val name: String) {

    override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean =
        this === other || (other is Topic<*, *> && other.name == name)

    override fun hashCode(): Int = name.hashCode()

    override fun toString(): String = "Topic($name)"

    companion object {
        /** A topic named [name] with payload type [T] and subject type [S]. */
        @JvmStatic
        fun <T, S> of(name: String): Topic<T, S> = Topic(name)

        /**
         * An unscoped (global) topic named [name]. Every session that subscribes
         * with `topic(key, initial)` receives publishes; sessions that never
         * subscribe are untouched.
         */
        @JvmStatic
        fun <T> global(name: String): Topic<T, GlobalSubject> = Topic(name)
    }
}

/** Kotlin-friendly alias for an unscoped (global) topic. */
typealias GlobalTopic<T> = Topic<T, GlobalSubject>

package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol

/**
 * A fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode (little-endian):
 *
 * `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]`
 *
 * The component-named methods preserve the Java record accessor API
 * (`op.category()`, `op.b()`, …) used by the renderers, hosts, and tests.
 */
data class Opcode(
    val category: Int,
    val command: Int,
    val flags: Int,
    val a: Int,
    val b: Int,
    val c: Int,
) {
    fun category(): Int = category
    fun command(): Int = command
    fun flags(): Int = flags
    fun a(): Int = a
    fun b(): Int = b
    fun c(): Int = c

    /** Serialize to the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
    fun toBytes(): ByteArray {
        val out = ByteArray(SIZE)
        out[0] = category.toByte()
        out[1] = command.toByte()
        out[2] = flags.toByte()
        out[3] = (flags ushr 8).toByte()
        writeIntLE(out, 4, a)
        writeIntLE(out, 8, b)
        writeIntLE(out, 12, c)
        return out
    }

    companion object {
        const val SIZE = 16

        /** Deserialize from the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
        fun fromBytes(bytes: ByteArray): Opcode {
            require(bytes.size == SIZE) { "opcode must be $SIZE bytes" }
            return Opcode(
                bytes[0].toInt() and 0xFF,
                bytes[1].toInt() and 0xFF,
                (bytes[2].toInt() and 0xFF) or ((bytes[3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 4),
                readIntLE(bytes, 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 12),
            )
        }

        private fun writeIntLE(out: ByteArray, offset: Int, value: Int) {
            out[offset] = value.toByte()
            out[offset + 1] = (value ushr 8).toByte()
            out[offset + 2] = (value ushr 16).toByte()
            out[offset + 3] = (value ushr 24).toByte()
        }

        private fun readIntLE(bytes: ByteArray, offset: Int): Int =
            (bytes[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
                ((bytes[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
                ((bytes[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
                ((bytes[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
    }
}

import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Commands

    val target: Int,
    val flags: Int,
    val x: Float,
    val y: Float,
    val value: Float,
    val text: String?,
    val b: Int,
    val c: Int,
) {
    fun command(): Int = command
    fun target(): Int = target

    fun x(): Float = x
    fun y(): Float = y
    fun value(): Float = value
    fun text(): String? = text
    fun b(): Int = b
    fun c(): Int = c

    val isPointerDown: Boolean
        get() = command == Commands.Event.POINTER_DOWN
    val isPointerMove: Boolean
        get() = command == Commands.Event.POINTER_MOVE
    val isPointerUp: Boolean
        get() = command == Commands.Event.POINTER_UP
    val isKeyDown: Boolean
        get() = command == Commands.Event.KEY_DOWN
    val isKeyUp: Boolean
        get() = command == Commands.Event.KEY_UP

    val isTextChanged: Boolean
        get() = command == Commands.Event.TEXT_CHANGED
    val isFocusChanged: Boolean

    val isEditingChanged: Boolean

    val isSubmit: Boolean

    val isScroll: Boolean

    val isWheel: Boolean

    val isFitChanged: Boolean
        get() = command == Commands.Event.FIT_CHANGED

    fun mediaPlaying(): Boolean = b != 0
    fun mediaValue(): Float = value
    fun fitIndex(): Int = Math.round(value)
    fun url(): String? = text
    val isNavigateBack: Boolean

    fun keyCode(): Int = b

        fun textChanged(target: Int, text: String?) =
            Event(Commands.Event.TEXT_CHANGED, target, 0, 0f, 0f, 0f, text, 0, 0)

        @JvmStatic
        fun focusChanged(target: Int, focused: Boolean) =
            Event(Commands.Event.FOCUS_CHANGED, target, 0, 0f, 0f, 0f, null, if (focused) 1 else 0, 0)

        @JvmStatic
        fun editingChanged(target: Int, editing: Boolean) =

            Event(Commands.Event.MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED, target, 0, 0f, 0f, seconds, null, 0, 0)

9: /** A declarative path → destination table with params and guards. */
10: class RouteTable private constructor(
11:     private val entries: List<Entry>,
12:     private val fallback: RouteHandler?,
13: ) {
14:     /** Match an absolute path, returning the first match or the fallback. */
15:     fun match(path: String): Optional<RouteMatch> {
16:         val pathOnly = Route.of(path).pathOnly()
17:         for (entry in entries) {
18:             val params = entry.match(pathOnly)
19:             if (!params.isPresent) continue
20:             val captured = params.get()
21:             if (entry.guard != null && !entry.guard.test(captured)) {
22:                 return Optional.of(RouteMatch.redirect(entry.redirect))
23:             }
24:             return Optional.of(RouteMatch(pathOnly, captured, entry.handler, null))
25:         }
26:         return if (fallback != null) {
27:             Optional.of(RouteMatch(pathOnly, Params.none(), fallback, null))
28:         } else {
29:             Optional.empty()
30:         }
31:     }
32: 
33:     /** A match: either a destination (handler + params) or a guard redirect. */
34:     data class RouteMatch(
35:         val path: String?,
36:         val params: Params,
37:         val handler: RouteHandler?,
38:         val redirect: String?,
39:     ) {
40:         fun path(): String? = path
41:         fun params(): Params = params
42:         fun handler(): RouteHandler? = handler
43:         fun redirect(): String? = redirect
44: 
45:         /** True when a guard redirected this match (replace, not mount). */
46:         fun isRedirect(): Boolean = redirect != null
47: 
48:         companion object {

55:     class Builder {
56:         private val entries = ArrayList<Entry>()
57:         private var fallback: RouteHandler? = null
58: 
59:         fun route(pattern: String, view: View): Builder {
60:             entries.add(Entry(pattern, RouteHandler { view }, null, null))
61:             return this
62:         }

64:         fun route(pattern: String, handler: RouteHandler): Builder {
65:             entries.add(Entry(pattern, handler, null, null))
66:             return this
67:         }

70:             entries.add(Entry(pattern, RouteHandler { view }, Objects.requireNonNull(guard, "guard"), redirect))
71:             return this
72:         }
73: 
74:         fun route(pattern: String, guard: Predicate<Params>, redirect: String?, handler: RouteHandler): Builder {

8: /** Converts a reactive signal's value into the typed property value stored on a node. */
9: object ReactiveValues {
10:     /** Read the signal for an initial render value without subscribing the component. */
11:     fun initial(property: Int, signal: Signal<*>): Any? =
12:         Signals.untracked { from(property, signal) }
13: 
14:     /** Read the signal and normalize its value for storage as a node property. */
15:     fun from(property: Int, signal: Signal<*>): Any? {
16:         var value: Any? = signal.get()
17:         if (value is Boolean) {
18:             value = if (value) 1 else 0
19:         } else if (value is WireValue) {
20:             value = value.wire()
21:         }
22:         return coerce(property, value)
23:     }
24: 
25:     private fun coerce(property: Int, value: Any?): Any? =
26:         when (ValueTypes.forProperty(property)) {
27:             ValueTypes.F32 -> toFloat(property, value)
28:             ValueTypes.U8, ValueTypes.U32, ValueTypes.I32, ValueTypes.ENUM -> toInt(property, value)
29:             ValueTypes.COLOR, ValueTypes.STRING, ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN -> value
30:             else -> value
31:         }
32: 
33:     private fun toFloat(property: Int, value: Any?): Float = when (value) {
34:         is Float -> value
35:         is Int -> value.toFloat()
36:         is Double -> value.toFloat()
37:         else -> throw unsupported(property, value)
38:     }
39: 
40:     private fun toInt(property: Int, value: Any?): Int = when (value) {
41:         is Int -> value
42:         is Float -> value.toInt()
43:         else -> throw unsupported(property, value)
44:     }
45:

47:         IllegalArgumentException(
48:             "Unsupported reactive property value $value for property 0x${Integer.toHexString(property)}",
49:         )

Notice `Environment.value(...)` static method used in DSL; Java class Environment can expose static `value`. Fine.

Important: DSL `Signals.kt` defines extension property `val <T> Signal<T>.value` and `var <T> WritableSignal<T>.value`. Kotlin extension properties on a Java interface are fine.

- The Maven build/lint/test workflow.
- How to move tests to new module: the core tests (SignalsTest.java, PersistentStateTest.java, FrameCodecTest.java, ProtocolManifestTest.java) should move; DSL tests (DslTest, EngineTraceTest, MediaProjectionTest, SignalsStateTest.kt, MarkdownTest.java?) Markdown currently in view-core; Markdown is non-DSL; should it move to pathland-core or stay? User chose all non-DSL packages. Markdown package `dev.pathland.markdown` is non-DSL. It depends on AttributedString (moving to core). So Markdown should move to core too, and its test. That means pathland-core needs Java only (Markdown is already Java). Good.

But `dev.pathland.view.dsl` currently imports `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown`. It will depend on core. Fine.

- Other modules importing specific classes. We need to update imports to `dev.pathland.core.*` and add `pathland-core` dependency where needed. Since package renamed, all downstream sources referencing `dev.pathland.view.core`/`dev.pathland.view.engine` need import updates. Let me quantify downstream usage by package to plan. Earlier list shows ~ many. Need to update all.

- `pathland-view-core` will keep `dev.pathland.view.dsl` and possibly a few core-ish classes? The user wants all non-DSL in core. So view-core only `dev.pathland.view.dsl` + tests. But note some DSL-adjacent classes currently in `dev.pathland.view.core` are themselves Views/modifiers (EnvironmentView, PathChangeView, PointerEventsView, TapGestureView, ReactiveSlotView, Modified, WindowMetadata, MediaController, Color, etc.). These are "core SPI/value types" and stay in core per choice. But then pathland-core contains View SPI + engine; view-core DSL is a thin layer. That's consistent.

# The demo modules live in the default-active `demos` profile. Activating
      # `release` deactivates it, so the reactor contains only publishable modules
      # (central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles every reactor module).
      - name: Deploy to Maven Central
        working-directory: lib/java
        env:
          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: mvn -B -P release deploy

      - name: Collect the published main jars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist/jars
          for m in pathland-view-core pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus \
                   pathland-quarkus-deployment; do
            cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
          ls -la dist/jars

      - name: Upload the main jars
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: jars
          path: dist/jars/*.jar
          if-no-files-found: error

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

**Premise correction:** the protocol engine is *already* Kotlin on the JVM. `pathland-view-core` implements opcodes, the diff emitter, signals, the `PLPL` codec, and is byte-checked against Rust by `ProtocolManifestTest` + `EngineTraceTest`. The JVM server path only pulls in **two** Rust dylibs through JNA:

- `libpathland_render_html` (`pathland-render-html`, ~5.9k LOC) — the real question
- `libpathland_markdown` (`pathland-markdown`, ~520 LOC)

So this is not "Rust protocol vs Kotlin protocol"; it's "keep the SSR HTML renderer in Rust, or reimplement it in Kotlin." The renderer is a pure function of the frame and depends only on `pathland-core`/`pathland-core-transport`, so a port is mechanically feasible.

## Does GraalVM care? Yes — mainly packaging, not speed

Today nothing targets native-image: CI is JVM-only and the Quarkus `Dockerfile` ships a JRE + jars. If you add Quarkus/Spring native later:

- **JNA itself works** under `native-image` (JNA 5.14 ships metadata), but it is not zero-config: reachability/reflection for the `Library` interface plus resource registration for the embedded dylib.
- The jar-extraction path (`getResourceAsStream("/META-INF/native/...")` → temp dir) needs `quarkus.native.resources.includes=META-INF/native/**`, and breaks in hardened containers with read-only/noexec `/tmp`.
- Avoiding extraction means shipping the `.so`/`.dylib` beside the executable and setting `-Dpathland.render.html.lib=...` — which forfeits the "single binary" benefit native images are for.
- A **pure Kotlin renderer** AOT-compiles in: no JNA, no dlopen, no resource extraction, no sidecar lib, one executable. That is a genuine operational difference.
- Runtime performance is a wash (the Rust code is already native); only minor JNA startup/init differs.

## Tradeoffs of porting

- Output must stay **byte-identical**: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-html-golden` treats Rust SSR as canonical and the TS DOM client asserts the same fixtures. A Kotlin port needs a golden test against those fixtures before it can be trusted.
- It creates a second SSR implementation. The repo deliberately removed the Java renderer (`e9aade28`) for a "single renderer, every language" story. The Rust crate is still the cross-language/C-ABI projection target for non-JVM hosts.
- Feature velocity: every new component/property must land in both renderers (mitigated by the golden harness — the TS client already proves cross-renderer drift is testable).

## Recommendation

- **If GraalVM native is on the roadmap now:** port `pathland-render-html` to Kotlin in the JVM module, keep the Rust crate for non-JVM hosts, and wire `pathland-html-golden` into both (port `pathland-markdown` too — it's tiny). This gives you true single-binary native images.
- **If native is speculative:** don't port. Keep the one Rust renderer and add native-image config only when needed (resource include + `pathland.render.html.lib` sidecar). Porting now is a large change for no current deployment gain.
- The protocol should stay where it is (Kotlin on the JVM, Rust canonical for non-JVM); there is no benefit to moving that.

**Premise correction:** the protocol engine is *already* Kotlin on the JVM. `pathland-view-core` implements opcodes, the diff emitter, signals, the `PLPL` codec, and is byte-checked against Rust by `ProtocolManifestTest` + `EngineTraceTest`. The JVM server path only pulls in **two** Rust dylibs through JNA:

- `libpathland_render_html` (`pathland-render-html`, ~5.9k LOC) — the real question
- `libpathland_markdown` (`pathland-markdown`, ~520 LOC)

So this is not "Rust protocol vs Kotlin protocol"; it's "keep the SSR HTML renderer in Rust, or reimplement it in Kotlin." The renderer is a pure function of the frame and depends only on `pathland-core`/`pathland-core-transport`, so a port is mechanically feasible.

## Does GraalVM care? Yes — mainly packaging, not speed

Today nothing targets native-image: CI is JVM-only and the Quarkus `Dockerfile` ships a JRE + jars. If you add Quarkus/Spring native later:

- **JNA itself works** under `native-image` (JNA 5.14 ships metadata), but it is not zero-config: reachability/reflection for the `Library` interface plus resource registration for the embedded dylib.
- The jar-extraction path (`getResourceAsStream("/META-INF/native/...")` → temp dir) needs `quarkus.native.resources.includes=META-INF/native/**`, and breaks in hardened containers with read-only/noexec `/tmp`.
- Avoiding extraction means shipping the `.so`/`.dylib` beside the executable and setting `-Dpathland.render.html.lib=...` — which forfeits the "single binary" benefit native images are for.
- A **pure Kotlin renderer** AOT-compiles in: no JNA, no dlopen, no resource extraction, no sidecar lib, one executable. That is a genuine operational difference.
- Runtime performance is a wash (the Rust code is already native); only minor JNA startup/init differs.

## Tradeoffs of porting

- Output must stay **byte-identical**: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-html-golden` treats Rust SSR as canonical and the TS DOM client asserts the same fixtures. A Kotlin port needs a golden test against those fixtures before it can be trusted.
- It creates a second SSR implementation. The repo deliberately removed the Java renderer (`e9aade28`) for a "single renderer, every language" story. The Rust crate is still the cross-language/C-ABI projection target for non-JVM hosts.
- Feature velocity: every new component/property must land in both renderers (mitigated by the golden harness — the TS client already proves cross-renderer drift is testable).

## Recommendation

- **If GraalVM native is on the roadmap now:** port `pathland-render-html` to Kotlin in the JVM module, keep the Rust crate for non-JVM hosts, and wire `pathland-html-golden` into both (port `pathland-markdown` too — it's tiny). This gives you true single-binary native images.
- **If native is speculative:** don't port. Keep the one Rust renderer and add native-image config only when needed (resource include + `pathland.render.html.lib` sidecar). Porting now is a large change for no current deployment gain.
- The protocol should stay where it is (Kotlin on the JVM, Rust canonical for non-JVM); there is no benefit to moving that.

When applied to annotation class X specifies that X defines a DSL language

Now, I don't need to ask about that. I'll include it as the approach with a note: add `kotlin-stdlib` as `provided` to pathland-core solely for `@kotlin.DslMarker` (or make it compile-only?) Actually Java compilation of the annotation requires the class, so `provided` is enough. At runtime, retention BINARY (CLASS) so not needed, but pathland-view-core brings stdlib anyway.

Let me ask a final question about Markdown and maybe about `GlobalTopic`. Actually, the plan can say: "Move Markdown to pathland-core under `dev.pathland.core.markdown` (per your rename choice); `GlobalTopic` typealias is unused and will be dropped." That's fine and consistent. If the user disagrees, they'll say.

One more thing: the engine is currently `dev.pathland.view.engine`; rename to `dev.pathland.core.engine`. Should the engine perhaps be `dev.pathland.core` directly (since it's core)? User said rename to dev.pathland.core.*; `dev.pathland.core.engine` is reasonable.

The comment "When the remaining non-DSL Kotlin is converted to Java..." can be updated/removed since non-DSL is gone but DSL remains; the reason for Dokka remains. The new module pathland-core uses JDK javadoc.

Now, potential issue: `mvn -P release` includes all reactor modules; pathland-core pure Java gets javadoc. Good.

Now, the build ordering: add module before view-core in parent `<modules>`. Maven topologically sorts anyway.

Now, source file inventory. Let me produce a grouped list:

`dev.pathland.core.protocol` (10): Categories, Commands, Components, Opcode, Properties, TokenPath, ValueEncoder, ValueTypes, WireValue. (9 actually)

- Keep in view-core: DslTest.kt, EngineTraceTest.kt, MediaProjectionTest.kt (imports updated).

parts.text:
Important finding: `GoldenConformanceTest.kt:43: val combined = base.copy(opcodes = base.opcodes + change.opcodes)` — uses `ProtocolFrame.copy(...)` data class copy. If `ProtocolFrame` becomes Java, `.copy()` and named arg disappear → must update that test. That's a concrete downside to note (only one occurrence).

Named args: most are DSL functions in `view-core`/demo which remain Kotlin (VStack, Button, ProxyView, Text, etc.). Core-converted constructors aren't called with named args in DSL/apps. Good. However `ProxyView(endpoint = adUrl, route = "/")` is a DSL function (stays Kotlin). Fine.

Destructuring: DslTest destructures `mount` return (Pair), not core data class. Fine. `val (result, frame)` is Kotlin Pair. No core destructuring.

`when` on core enum: only on `children.size`, not enums. Good.

Nullability: many core APIs return nullable. Without annotations, Kotlin sees platform types, which weakens safety but existing code uses `?.`, `?:` which still compile. The issue is Kotlin overriding Java `makeBody` returning `View?`: Kotlin can override with nullable type? When overriding a Java method with platform return type, Kotlin allows either nullable or non-null return. So `override fun makeBody(...): View?` is fine. But nullability checks are weakened. Also Kotlin's `config.label()?.let` works. Fine.

Real downsides to articulate:

1. **Loss of named arguments & default arguments** for moved core constructors/functions. Concrete: `ProtocolFrame.copy(opcodes = ...)` in GoldenConformanceTest must be rewritten; `TextAttribute(property, value)` default `valueType` must become explicit overloads. Kotlin cannot use named args with Java methods/constructors, so app code that constructs core types with named args (none found in repo, but external users might) breaks. Since packages are renamed anyway, it's a source break, but ergonomics permanently decline.

2. **Loss of `copy()`/destructuring/`componentN()`** on core data classes. Only GoldenConformanceTest uses `.copy`. External users lose it. Mitigation: add explicit `withX`/`copy` factory methods or keep a thin Kotlin wrapper? Not worth it.

3. **Weakened null-safety at the Kotlin↔Java boundary.** Without nullability annotations, Java returns/params become *platform types* (`String!`, `View!`). Kotlin stops enforcing null checks, permits unsafe calls, and smart casts can be less reliable. Mitigation: annotate Java with JSpecify/JetBrains `@Nullable/@NonNull` (adds a dependency) or accept the softening.

4. **No declaration-site variance / Kotlin-specific generics.** Java types lose Kotlin `out` variance, sealed hierarchies, reified/inline helpers. Current core has little variance, but `Signal<*>`/`Topic<T,S>` cross the boundary as platform generics; type inference may require explicit types/casts. Also `Topic` companion factory `Topic.of` etc.

5. **`when` exhaustiveness** over Java enums is not checked (Kotlin treats Java enums as non-exhaustive). Core enums (NavOp/ThemeMode/…) used in `when` lose compile-time exhaustiveness. Currently DSL doesn't `when` on them, but future DSL code will.

6. **Operators/extension ergonomics**: Java methods aren't operators (`Params.get` indexing gone). Extension functions can still be defined in the Kotlin DSL module, so `.value`, `.map`, etc. remain.

7. **Kotlin-only constructs disappear from core**: `typealias GlobalTopic` removed; `object` singletons become `INSTANCE` (GlobalSubject); companion object factories become statics; Kotlin `internal` semantics become package-private/public (no module-wide internal). This can widen API unintentionally.

8. **Two-module build and IDE complexity**: more Maven modules, cross-module navigation; Kotlin sees Java sources with no Kotlin metadata (no default params, no nullability, no extension resolution). Debugging crosses language boundaries. Rebuild order.

9. **Function types/callbacks**: Kotlin lambdas passed to Java functional interfaces still work via SAM, but Kotlin-specific function types (`() -> T`) vs `Supplier<T>` can add wrapping; `unit`-returning lambdas map to `Runnable`; overloads may become ambiguous. Let me draft with concrete, recent findings.

Short answer: the **view-building DSL stays Kotlin**, so authoring `VStack { Text(...) }` is unchanged. The downsides are at the **Kotlin→Java boundary** you cross whenever the DSL/app touches core types.

## Concrete downsides for Kotlin view authors

1. **No named or default arguments on core APIs.** Kotlin cannot use named args with Java constructors/methods, and Java has no default params.
   - `TextAttribute(property, valueType = …)` loses its default.
   - Any app code constructing `Color`, `Length`, `Route`, `Event`, `Opcode`, `ProtocolFrame`, `EffectOptions` with named args breaks (none found in-repo, but external users would).
   - Mitigation: add Java overloads/factories; accept that named args are gone.

2. **`copy()` and destructuring disappear on core data classes.** `base.copy(opcodes = …)` at `lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/test/kotlin/.../GoldenConformanceTest.kt:43` must become a factory/constructor call. No core destructuring found in-repo, but external code loses `componentN()`.

3. **Weakened null-safety.** Core is full of nullable Kotlin types (`Color.token: String?`, `View?` from styles, `AttributedString` text, etc.). Without annotations, Kotlin sees Java types as *platform types* (`String!`), so it stops enforcing null checks and smart casts can be less reliable.
   - Mitigation: annotate the Java core with JSpecify or JetBrains `@Nullable/@NonNull`. Adds a dependency and annotation work; otherwise the safety net is softer than today.

4. **No `when` exhaustiveness over core enums.** Kotlin does not exhaustiveness-check `when` over Java enums (`NavOp`, `ThemeMode`, `Chrome`, font/alignment enums, …). No current DSL `when` on these, but future code loses a compile-time guard.

5. **Kotlin-specific shapes become Java shapes.** `object GlobalSubject` becomes `INSTANCE` (call sites in `Signals.kt`/`dsl/Signals.kt` change); companion factories become statics; `typealias GlobalTopic` disappears; `operator fun Params.get` loses `params["x"]`; `internal` widens to public/package-private. Encapsulation and ergonomics are slightly worse.

6. **Less precise generic inference.** Java has no declaration-site variance; `Signal<*>`, `Topic<T,S>`, `Signal<T>` returns become platform generics, so occasional explicit types/casts may be needed. Java overload pairs like `EnvironmentBinding.Config.value(Any?)` / `value(Signal<*>)` can also become ambiguous for `null`/platform values.

7. **Two-artifact/IDE friction.** More Maven wiring, cross-module navigation, and no Kotlin metadata (KDoc/default args) for core in the IDE. Dokka for `pathland-view-core` also won't naturally document the Java core.

8. **`@DslMarker` bridge.** `@PathlandDsl` becomes a Java annotation meta-annotated with `@kotlin.DslMarker` (Spring Integration does this, so it works), but it forces a `kotlin-stdlib` `provided` dependency into the “pure Java” core. If that ever breaks, you either keep one Kotlin file or lose the scope guard.

## What does **not** regress

- Builders/modifiers/`Component`/`Scope`/`ForEach` remain Kotlin.
- `signal`/`computed`/`effect`, `Signal { … }` SAM, `.value` extensions, `topic(...)`, and route DSL remain Kotlin-friendly.
- Java getters map to Kotlin properties, so `node.text`, `color.argb`, `value.isPlain` still work if we add `getX()`/`isX()`s.
- Runtime behavior, opcodes, and emission are unchanged; Java core may even be marginally better for native-image/javadoc.

## Practical takeaway

For **this repo**, the source churn is modest: zero core named-arg usages and one `.copy()` call were found. The lasting costs are **nullability softening**, **lost named/default/`copy` ergonomics**, **lost enum exhaustiveness**, and **`GlobalSubject`/`Params` shape changes** — all mitigable, but permanently less Kotlin-idiomatic than today.

If Kotlin authoring ergonomics are a top priority, the lower-risk alternative is to keep core in Kotlin and only split the artifact (`pathland-core` Kotlin + `pathland-view-core` DSL). You get the module boundary without any interoperability loss. The Java rewrite buys language-neutral core code/JDK javadoc, but costs the Kotlin-facing ergonomics above.

Good. FrameCodec has no AttributedString dependency. Event/EnvironmentData no. So the minimal Java wire module is clean if we exclude ValueEncoder? ValueEncoder imports Color, so if we move ValueEncoder, need ColorValue. We can either:
- Move ValueEncoder with a `ColorValue` interface (recommended; keeps protocol complete).
- Keep ValueEncoder in Kotlin (then `dev.pathland.core.protocol` misses ValueEncoder; `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink` stay Kotlin and import Kotlin ValueEncoder). Cleaner module but inconsistent package.
I'll recommend ColorValue seam and move ValueEncoder. It's a tiny interface:
```java
package dev.pathland.core.protocol;
public interface ColorValue { int argb(); }
```
`Color` (Kotlin) implements `ColorValue` (in addition to View, TokenPath). `ValueEncoder` uses `((ColorValue) value).argb()`. No behavior change. Note: Java `ColorValue` interface and Kotlin `Color` implements. Also `Color` is used by DSL; no change.
Alternatively name it `ArgbColor` or `ColorRef`. Use `ColorValue`.

Wait: `ValueEncoder` also handles `ValueTypes.COLOR` where value is a `Color`; if any other color-ish value is passed? Only Color. Fine.

Now, what about `WireValue`? Move. Kotlin enums implement it; no issue.

`TokenPath` move; Kotlin `Color`, `Length`, `FontFamily.Token` implement it. Fine.

`Opcode` toString/equals; Java implement.

`Event` data class: Java class with public fields? Currently Kotlin data class with private fields and methods `command()` etc.; Kotlin FrameCodec uses `.command`, `.target`, `.flags`, `.text`, `.value`, `.b`, `.c`, `.x`, `.y` properties (behind getCommand etc.). If Event becomes Java with explicit `command()` methods and `getCommand()` getters? To keep Kotlin FrameCodec (which will be moved to Java) no issue, but other Kotlin code may access `.command` etc. Let's check usages of Event properties in Kotlin outside transport. `Emitter` uses `event.target()` etc. `InputDispatcher` uses methods. `Router.handleEvent` uses `event.isNavigateBack`, `event.url()`. So methods. But maybe tests use `.text`. To be safe, Java Event exposes:
- constructor `Event(int command, int target, int flags, float x, float y, float value, String text, int b, int c)`
- methods `command()`, `target()`, etc.
- getters `getCommand()` etc.? Kotlin property `.command` is not used outside? Let's check `event.` usage in Kotlin for Event.

Good. Kotlin `FrameCodec` uses Event properties; we'll port FrameCodec to Java so no Kotlin property access. Other Kotlin code uses methods. `Event` Java should still expose getters for potential Kotlin property access? Search found only FrameCodec uses property access. So methods suffice, but we can add getters for safety. `ProtocolFrame` Kotlin property access in GoldenConformanceTest line 43 (`base.opcodes`, `change.opcodes`) → if ProtocolFrame Java, `getOpcodes()` gives `.opcodes` property, so `base.opcodes` still works; `.copy` fails. Good.

`Opcode` property access only in Kotlin FrameCodec (`op.category`, `op.command`, `op.a`, `op.b`, `op.flags` etc.) → we port FrameCodec to Java, so no Kotlin. Tests use methods. Good. `Event` property access only FrameCodec. Good.

`EnvironmentData` property access in Kotlin FrameCodec (`env.route`, `env.viewportWidth`) → ported to Java. Java callers use methods. Good.

So moving wire classes is straightforward.

Now, decide on `ValueEncoder` and `ColorValue`. If we move ValueEncoder to Java, the Java module needs `ColorValue` interface. Kotlin `Color` (stays) implements `ColorValue`. `FrameOpcodeSink` (stays Kotlin) imports Java ValueEncoder and passes `Color` (implements ColorValue) → Java method signature `encodeBits(int, Object)` casts to `ColorValue`. Fine. `RingOpcodeSink` (native-core Kotlin) imports Java ValueEncoder; passes values. Fine.
- Note `ValueEncoder.encodeBits` signature currently `(valueType: Int, value: Any): Int`. Java: `public static int encodeBits(int valueType, Object value)`. Kotlin calls `ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value)` fine (Object param accepts Any). For COLOR, casts to `ColorValue`.
- `Color` implements `ColorValue`: add `dev.pathland.core.protocol.ColorValue` to its implements list, `override fun argb(): Int` already exists. Kotlin can implement Java interface. Good.

So Java module can have protocol + wire transport (excluding OpcodeSink/FrameOpcodeSink). `AttributedString` stays Kotlin. Then `OpcodeSink`/`FrameOpcodeSink` stay in `dev.pathland.view.core.transport`. But `FrameCodec` moves to `dev.pathland.core.transport`; tests need update. `FrameOpcodeSink` stays and still has `frame(): ProtocolFrame` returning Java ProtocolFrame. Fine.

+package dev.pathland.core.protocol;
+
+/** Value types for {@code PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY} (mirrors {@code pathland_core::value_type}). */
+public final class ValueTypes {
+    public static final int U8 = 0x01;
+    public static final int U32 = 0x02;
+    public static final int I32 = 0x03;
+    public static final int F32 = 0x04;
+    public static final int STRING = 0x05;
+    public static final int ENUM = 0x06;
+    public static final int COLOR = 0x07;
+    public static final int DESIGN_TOKEN = 0x08;
+    public static final int LIST = 0x09;
+
+    private ValueTypes() {
+    }
+
+    /** The protocol value type for a property id (mirrors {@code value_type_for}). */
+    public static int forProperty(int prop) {
+        switch (prop) {
+            case Properties.COLOR:
+            case Properties.BACKGROUND_COLOR:
+            case Properties.BORDER_COLOR:
+            case Properties.COLOR_MULTIPLY:
+            case Properties.SHADOW_COLOR:
+            case Properties.COLOR_VALUE:
+            case Properties.TINT:
+                return COLOR;
+            case Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS:
+            case Properties.BORDER_EDGES:
+                return U32;
+            case Properties.SELECTED:
+            case Properties.VISIBLE:
+            case Properties.ENABLED:
+            case Properties.UNDERLINE:
+            case Properties.STRIKETHROUGH:
+            case Properties.COLOR_INVERT:
+            case Properties.CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS:
+            case Properties.ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING:
+            case Properties.IS_SECURE:
+            case Properties.IS_INDETERMINATE:
+            case Properties.FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL:
+            case Properties.FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL:
+            case Properties.MEDIA_MUTED:
+            case Properties.MEDIA_LOOP:
+                return U8;
+            case Properties.LABEL:
+            case Properties.PROMPT:
+            case Properties.FONT_FAMILY:
+            case Properties.IMAGE_SOURCE:
+            case Properties.MEDIA_SOURCE:
+            case Properties.ROUTE:
+            case Properties.ICON_NAME:
+            case Properties.GRID_TRACKS:
+                return STRING;
+            case Properties.LINE_LIMIT:
+            case Properties.SELECTION:
+            case Properties.ACTION_ID:
+            case Properties.BINDING_ID:
+            case Properties.NAV_DEPTH:
+            case Properties.PLAYBACK_STATE:
+            case Properties.MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID:
+                return U32;
+            case Properties.FIT_QUERY:
+                return LIST;
+            case Properties.ALIGNMENT:
+            case Properties.TEXT_ALIGNMENT:
+            case Properties.TRUNCATION_MODE:
+            case Properties.TEXT_CASE:
+            case Properties.FONT_STYLE:
+            case Properties.FONT_DESIGN:

+            case Properties.SHAPE_KIND:
+            case Properties.DATE_PICKER_MODE:
+            case Properties.PICKER_STYLE:
+            case Properties.TOGGLE_STYLE:
+                return F32;
+            default:
+                return F32;
+        }
+    }

          GTK/Qt renderer dylibs) and for regenerating shared artifacts (the protocol
          manifest, engine traces, HTML golden fixtures, and TS constants).
 
          Run BEFORE an IntelliJ IDE run: refreshes the generated layers the IDE cannot
          rebuild itself — the design CSS/tokens (npm build) and the DOM bundle
          (npm build:all) — plus the render-html module's embedded CSS resources (its
          Maven copy step does not run under IntelliJ's own build). IntelliJ then
          compiles the Java modules from its module outputs (the pathland modules are
          imported, so no ~/.m2 is used) and copies the refreshed bundle + its
          dom-renderer.current manifest into target/classes on Build Project. Invoke with
          `mvn -P refresh-ide validate`, then Reload All Maven Projects → Build → Run →
          reload. The bundle is content-hashed (dom-renderer-<sha256>.js) so a rebuilt
          bundle busts the immutable asset cache by URL — a normal reload after restart
          is enough, no hard refresh. -->
     <profiles>
     <!-- Default reactor: the libraries plus the demo applications. Maven deactivates
          an activeByDefault profile as soon as any other profile in this POM is
          activated, so `-P release`, `-P refresh-ide`, and `-P jvm-only` all leave a
          demo-free reactor. -->
     <profile>
         <id>demos</id>
         <activation>
             <activeByDefault>true</activeByDefault>
         </activation>
         <modules>
             <module>pathland-demo-views-kotlin</module>
             <module>pathland-desktop-demo</module>
             <module>pathland-quarkus-demo</module>
             <module>pathland-spring-boot-demo</module>
         </modules>
     </profile>
     <!-- `mvn -Pjvm-only test`: the JVM libraries and server starters only. Activating
          this profile deactivates the default-active `demos` profile, so no demo
          modules are in the reactor. The JVM libraries never required Rust. -->
     <profile>
         <id>jvm-only</id>
         <properties>
             <pathland.jvm-only>true</pathland.jvm-only>
         </properties>
     </profile>
     <!-- Maven Central publishing (`mvn -P release deploy`). Normal builds/tests are
          unaffected: this profile only activates on demand. Because it is active, the
          default `demos` profile is off and the reactor contains only publishable
          modules. -->
     <profile>
         <id>release</id>
         <build>
             <plugins>
                 <plugin>
                     <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                     <artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
                     <version>3.3.1</version>
                     <executions>
                         <execution>
                             <id>attach-sources</id>
                             <goals><goal>jar-no-fork</goal></goals>
                         </execution>
                     </executions>
                 </plugin>
                 <plugin>
                     <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                     <artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId>
                     <version>3.6.3</version>
                     <configuration>
                         <!-- Central requires a -javadoc jar; disable strict doclint so
                              existing doc comments don't fail the release build.
                              Don't link to reactor siblings' apidocs: pathland-view-core
                              builds its javadoc with Dokka, so target/apidocs does not
                              exist and javadoc logs "Error fetching link" noise. -->
                         <doclint>none</doclint>
                         <detectOfflineLinks>false</detectOfflineLinks>
                     </configuration>
                     <executions>
                         <execution>
                             <id>attach-javadocs</id>
                             <goals><goal>jar</goal></goals>
                         </execution>
                     </executions>
                 </plugin>
                 <plugin>
                     <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                     <artifactId>maven-gpg-plugin</artifactId>
                     <version>3.2.4</version>
                     <executions>
                         <execution>
                             <id>sign-artifacts</id>
                             <phase>verify</phase>
                             <goals><goal>sign</goal></goals>
                         </execution>
                     </executions>
                 </plugin>
                 <!-- Uploads the whole reactor to the Sonatype Central Portal as one
                      deployment (auto-published after validation). Credentials come
                      from the `central` server in ~/.m2/settings.xml. -->

                     <groupId>org.sonatype.central</groupId>
                     <artifactId>central-publishing-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                     <version>0.6.0</version>

Index: .github/workflows/release.yml
===================================================================
--- .github/workflows/release.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/release.yml	
@@ -1,250 +1,250 @@
 name: Release
 
 # Publishing a GitHub Release (which creates the tag, e.g. `v0.1.1`) builds and
 # publishes every artifact — the Rust crates to crates.io and the Java libraries
 # to Maven Central (with the renderer's native libraries for every supported
 # platform) — then attaches the built files to the Release.
 #
 # The tag drives the version: the workflow writes the tag's `X.Y.Z` into the Rust
 # workspace version and the Java parent version (in CI only) before building, and
 # a `bump` job commits that version back to `main` afterwards. No pre-bump commit
 # is required. Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release
 # suffix is allowed).
 #
 # The publish steps are idempotent, so re-running a partially failed release is
 # safe (a crate+version already on crates.io is skipped; Maven Central rejects a
 # re-deploy of an existing version).
 #
 # Secrets:
 #   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN  crates.io API token (publish scope)
 #   GPG_PRIVATE_KEY       armored GPG private key (signing)
 #   GPG_PASSPHRASE        its passphrase
 #   CENTRAL_USERNAME      Sonatype Central Portal user token username
 #   CENTRAL_PASSWORD      Sonatype Central Portal user token password
 
 on:
   release:
     types: [published]
   workflow_dispatch:
     inputs:
       tag:
         description: 'Tag to release (e.g. v0.1.1); blank = current ref'
         required: false
 
 permissions:
   contents: write
 
 jobs:
   version:
     name: Resolve + validate version
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     outputs:
       tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
       version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
     steps:
       - id: v
         name: Derive the version from the tag
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           tag="${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
           if [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
             echo "::error::tag '$tag' must be v<major>.<minor>.<patch>"
             exit 1
           fi
           version="${tag#v}"
           echo "tag=$tag version=$version"
           echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
 
   rust:
     name: Publish crates to crates.io
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: version
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
       - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
 
       - name: Set the version from the tag
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           cargo install cargo-edit --locked
           cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
           # Sanity: the workspace version + the intra-workspace path-dep pins.
           awk -F'"' '/^version = /{print "workspace:", $2; exit}' Cargo.toml
           grep -rho 'pathland-[a-z-]*", version = "[^"]*"' crates/*/Cargo.toml | sort -u
 
       - name: Test the publishable crates
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-markdown -p pathland-engine -p pathland-view -p pathland-render-core -p pathland-core-transport -p pathland-render-html
 
       - name: Publish in dependency order
         working-directory: lib/rust
         env:
           CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
           crates=(pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-render-core pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html)
           for c in "${crates[@]}"; do
             echo "::group::publish $c $version"
             # Idempotent: skip a crate+version already on crates.io.
             if curl -sf -A "pathland-release-ci" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c/$version" >/dev/null; then
               echo "$c $version already published — skipping"
               echo "::endgroup::"
               continue
             fi
             # `cargo publish` packages (leaving the .crate in target/package) then uploads.
             # `--allow-dirty`: `cargo set-version` above intentionally edits the
             # crates' manifests (the path-dep version pins), so the tree is "dirty".
             cargo publish --allow-dirty -p "$c"
             echo "::endgroup::"
             # Let the index propagate so the next dependent crate resolves it.
             sleep 20
           done
 
       - name: Package (guarantee .crate files for the release assets)
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           # All dependencies are published by now, so packaging every crate works.
           for c in pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-render-core pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html; do
             cargo package --allow-dirty -p "$c"
           done
 
       - name: Upload the .crate files
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: crates
           path: lib/rust/target/package/*.crate
           if-no-files-found: error
 
   java:
     name: Publish to Maven Central
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [version]
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
 
       - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
         uses: actions/setup-java@v4
         with:
           distribution: temurin
           java-version: '17'
           cache: maven
           server-id: central
           server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
           server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
           gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
           gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE
 
       # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
       # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
       # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
       # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
       - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           v=3.9.9
           curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
           echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
           mvn -v
 
       - name: Set the version from the tag
         working-directory: lib/java
         run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true
 
       # The demo modules live in the default-active `demos` profile. Activating
       # `release` deactivates it, so the reactor contains only publishable modules
       # (central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles every reactor module).
       - name: Deploy to Maven Central
         working-directory: lib/java
         env:
           CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
           CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
           MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
         run: mvn -B -P release deploy
 
       - name: Collect the published main jars
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           mkdir -p dist/jars
-          for m in pathland-view-core pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
+          for m in pathland-core pathland-view-core pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
                    pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus \
                    pathland-quarkus-deployment; do
             cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
           done
           rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
           ls -la dist/jars
 
       - name: Upload the main jars
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: jars
           path: dist/jars/*.jar
           if-no-files-found: error
 
   bump:
     name: Commit the version back to main
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [version, rust, java]
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: main
           fetch-depth: 0
 
       - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
       - name: Set the Rust version
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           cargo install cargo-edit --locked
           cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
 
       - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
         with:
           distribution: temurin
           java-version: '17'
       - name: Set the Java version
         working-directory: lib/java
         run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true
 
       - name: Commit + push
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
           git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
           if git diff --quiet; then
             echo "version already current on main — nothing to commit"
             exit 0
           fi
           git add -A
           git commit -m "chore(release): v${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
           git push origin HEAD:main
 
   release-assets:
     name: Attach release assets
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [version, rust, java]
     steps:
       - name: Download all build artifacts
         uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
         with:
           path: dist
 
       - name: Collect the files to attach
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           mkdir -p out
           find dist -type f \( -name '*.crate' -o -name '*.jar' -o -name '*.dll' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' \) -exec cp {} out/ \;
           ls -la out
 
       - name: Attach to the GitHub Release
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
         run: gh release upload "${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}" out/* --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --clobber
